dispute: Posed as: can a people who consume their dead be said to care about them as much as a people who bury theirs. Raised as a challenge to the option-distribution reading.
source: From a classroom exchange. First case in this repo not constructed by the model. Diverges from the other two: the smuggled content sits in the question's setup rather than in either side's position.

sides.position: burial indicates care; its absence indicates less care

option_claims.note: present in the account as an object of treatment
granted option generation, but the options are scored against the asker's practice set

held_fixed: the mapping from practice to interior disposition
which practices are available to score against

frame.boundary_criterion: the practice the asker recognises is the definition of the category

cuts_required.cut: how an unfamiliar practice is classified
how much care each recognised practice indicates

sides.position: consuming the dead is the practice by which the dead are kept with the living

option_claims.note: same position as in the asker's account
options scored against its own practice set

held_fixed: the mapping from practice to interior disposition

frame.boundary_criterion: the practice is read against the frame that assigns it meaning

cuts_required.cut: which frame assigns this practice its meaning

residue_candidates.claim: one people cares about its dead less than the other
residue_candidates.note: Stage 1 matches on every party: same tally, same optionality, same decision authority. The divergence is entirely at stage 2 — what the practice is scored against. This is the first case in the repo where the option layer matches and the disagreement is still accounted for.

residue_candidates.claim: the practice carries a transmission risk
residue_candidates.note: A public-health quantity, independently measurable, and not evidence about interior disposition. Recorded as separate rather than as residue: it is a real finding on a different quantity that the original framing welds into one verdict. Kept in the file so the separation is visible.

residue_candidates.claim: the question presupposes its own answer
residue_candidates.note: Not residue between the sides — a property of the setup. The asker's premise is the disputed mapping, so the question cannot be answered without granting it. Nearest structural relative of the shared-assumption item in means-to-save, but located in the question rather than in the two positions.
